subject: LucidHealth: Dedicated capacity decision (GPU shortlist + token mix confirmation)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Huang <claire@lucidhealth.com>, Anil Shah <anil@lucidhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + asks — deployment path & throughput clarifications

Thanks again for the productive conversation earlier — quick recap and the key asks so we can land a Dedicated proposal that meets LucidHealth's compliance and performance needs.

Summary of what we heard
- Primary priority: predictable latency for patient-facing clinical summarization API (SLA target: p95 < 300ms for short prompts).
- Compliance note: you prefer Private VPC for PHI but are open to Dedicated (isolated pool) if we can provide SOC2 evidence and a tight network boundary.
- Workload profile: mixed — many short prompts for triage (low tokens) and periodic long-generation tasks for full notes.

Key sizing inputs we need from you (please confirm each):
1) Average sustained TPS (inference requests per second) during normal hours
2) Peak TPS you expect during surges (brief spikes, ~10–30 minutes)
3) Token mix: average prompt tokens, average generated tokens, and percent distribution of short vs long requests
4) Desired concurrency (do you expect many simultaneous interactive sessions or mostly single-threaded batch jobs?)

Our initial guidance (based on the call):
- We recommend evaluating Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) as the preferred path for latency and isolation. Private VPC is viable but adds onboarding time and networking work. Hosted API is an option only if you accept less strict isolation.
- Short-term GPU shortlist to discuss: H100 (best peak throughput + latency), A100 (cost-effective for steady workloads), L4/L40S (good for smaller models or cost-sensitive endpoints).

Ask: can you confirm the numbers below so we can run a capacity worksheet and give an H100 vs A100 pod recommendation?
- Avg TPS: (please confirm) — we captured ~10–15 TPS from your demo but want firm numbers
- Peak TPS: (please confirm) — you mentioned occasional spikes up to a couple hundred?
- Token averages: prompt ~100–150 tokens, response ~250–400 tokens?

Attachments: lucid_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx (worksheet for you to drop actual traffic numbers), redwood_dedicated_pricing_summary.pdf (pricing breakouts by GPU class)

Next steps
- If you can fill the worksheet this week we’ll run a short sizing simulation and come back with 2 alternatives (cost-optimized A100 plan and performance-optimized H100 plan) plus an estimated rollout SOW for Private VPC if you decide to go that route.
- Proposed follow-up: 30-minute sizing review on Thursday or Friday.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

From: Claire Huang <claire@lucidhealth.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>
Cc: Anil Shah <anil@lucidhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + asks — deployment path & throughput clarifications

Thanks Grace — quick answers below. I filled the worksheet with a rough first pass and attached it in the Drive link (you can use that).

Confirmed numbers (rough, will update worksheet with exact hourly breakdowns):
- Average sustained TPS: 12 requests/sec across our EU/US regions during weekdays (non-peak)
- Expected peak TPS: ~240 requests/sec (these happen 2–3 times per week for 10–20 minutes during morning syncs)
- Token mix: ~72% short interactions (prompt ~60–120 tokens, response ~80–180 tokens), ~28% long jobs (prompt ~200–400 tokens, response ~400–1,200 tokens).
- Concurrency pattern: many simultaneous interactive sessions but requests are short; long jobs are asynchronous and can be queued.

Compliance: Our security team strongly prefers Private VPC if material PHI will be processed. If Dedicated can be delivered inside our VPC (private deployment) that would be ideal; otherwise Dedicated with strict network isolation is acceptable as an interim.

Happy to take the 30-minute review — Thursday 16:00 PT or Friday 10:00 PT works for our team.

Claire
Claire Huang
Head of Platform Integrations | LucidHealth
claire@lucidhealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Claire Huang <claire@lucidhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + asks — deployment path & throughput clarifications

Quick internal note following Claire's numbers — pulling rough sizing now. High-level thoughts:
- Peak 240 TPS with ~30% long job mix pushes the token throughput requirement. For low p95 latency on short prompts H100s give the best headroom.
- Ballpark starting config (redundant, supports peak): 2x H100 pods (each pod = 8xH100s or the configuration we typically provision), configured for continuous batching with a 6–8 req concurrency per GPU for short prompts; long jobs can be routed to a separate pool sized for throughput (could be A100 cluster to save cost).
- If LucidHealth prefers cost-first, an A100-dominant pool (3–4 A100 GPUs) with aggressive batching and caching could meet avg TPS but risks higher tail latency under spikes.

Action items for convo:
- Confirm whether long jobs can be scheduled into an async queue (helps reduce dedicated H100 count).
- Confirm SLA tolerance: is p95 300ms a hard target for ALL requests or only for short interactive flows?

I will sketch a proper H100 vs A100 cost/latency table for Thursday's review.

— Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Thanks Claire — this is exactly what we needed. Next steps and timeline:

1) I will run the worksheet with the numbers you confirmed and produce two concrete proposals by EOD Thursday:
   - Performance path: H100-dominant Dedicated pool with sizing for peak 240 TPS (redundancy + canary), expect rollout SOW for Private VPC option if you require it.
   - Cost path: A100-focused pool with async routing for long jobs and caching for short prompts.

2) I'll share a 30-minute slot for Thursday 16:00 PT and a calendar invite (I picked the slot you preferred). Please accept if that works; otherwise pick Friday 10:00 PT.

3) Deliverables on the call:
   - H100 vs A100 cost/latency table and recommended pod counts
   - Estimated monthly cost for Dedicated capacity (broken down per GPU class) and expected token cost savings from KV caching and batching
   - A short checklist of networking steps for Private VPC onboarding (what Lucid's infra team will need to prepare)

Links/attachments: capacity worksheet (Drive), redwood_dedicated_pricing_summary.pdf (attached), draft SOW link for Dedicated pools: https://docsend.com/s/rlw-dedicated-sow (we'll only send final after sizing)

If Claire confirms the worksheet is the final set of numbers we’ll include it in the sizing simulation; otherwise we can iterate after the Thursday call.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
